+- **GUI Apps on Linux** (`gui_apps` tag on `ubuntu_desktop`): [`gui_apps_linux`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml) bundles Alacritty (cargo), AppImageLauncher (PPA with `.deb` fallback, Lite variant for noRoot), VSCode (Microsoft apt repo), Cursor (`.deb`), Discord (Flatpak default or `.deb`), optional Steam via Valve apt repo when `installGamingApps=true`, Zen Browser (AppImage + `.desktop` entry for launcher search), and `libfuse2` for AppImage compatibility. macOS equivalents ship via [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl) (Arc + Discord + optional Steam casks there). See [docs/tools/appimage.md](docs/tools/appimage.md) for AppImageLauncher install paths, `ail-cli` usage, and Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor gotchas.
 - **niri** (optional, `installNiri=true`, `ubuntu_desktop` only): [niri](https://github.com/niri-wm/niri) scrollable-tiling Wayland compositor built from source via the [`niri`](dot_ansible/roles/niri/tasks/main.yml) ansible role (binary → `/usr/local/bin`, GDM session + systemd user units, NVIDIA VRAM application-profile when an NVIDIA GPU is present). Starter config at [`dot_config/niri/config.kdl`](dot_config/niri/config.kdl). Full guide: [docs/playbooks/niri.md](docs/playbooks/niri.md).
 - **AeroSpace** (macOS, with `installBrewApps=true`): [AeroSpace](https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) tiling window manager (cask in [`Brewfile.darwin.tmpl`](dot_config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin.tmpl)). Config is chezmoi-managed at the XDG path [`~/.config/aerospace/aerospace.toml`](dot_config/aerospace/aerospace.toml) (legacy `~/.aerospace.toml` is auto-removed via `.chezmoiremove` to avoid AeroSpace's both-configs-present error). macOS counterpart to niri on Linux — keybinds (alt + hjkl/arrows, `alt+enter` terminal) are aligned.
 - **Starship**: Cross-shell prompt (replaces oh-my-zsh theme)

+# =============================================================================
+# Steam — optional gaming bundle via Valve's official apt repository
+#
+# Gated by the `installGamingApps` chezmoi prompt, plumbed through
+# `gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps`. Valve's repo publishes an amd64
+# `steam-launcher` package and an i386 transitional package; adding i386 is
+# required so Steam can resolve its 32-bit runtime libraries. Avoid hard-coding
+# old package names like `libgl1-mesa-glx`, which no longer exists on Ubuntu
+# 24.04 — let apt resolve current dependencies/recommends from the package.
+# =============================================================================
+
+- name: Skip Steam on non-x86_64 Linux
+  when:
+    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
+    - gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps | bool
+    - target_architecture != 'x86_64'
+  ansible.builtin.debug:
+    msg: >-
+      Steam is only installed on x86_64 here. Valve's Ubuntu launcher and
+      game runtime expect amd64/i386 packages; skipping on {{ target_architecture }}.
+
+- name: Skip Steam in noRoot mode
+  when:
+    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
+    - gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps | bool
+    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
+    - gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool
+  ansible.builtin.debug:
+    msg: >-
+      installGamingApps=true, but Steam requires sudo to add Valve's apt repo,
+      enable i386, and install steam-launcher. Skipping in noRoot mode.
+
+- name: Install Steam via Valve apt repo
+  when:
+    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
+    - gui_apps_linux_install_gaming_apps | bool
+    - target_architecture == 'x86_64'
+    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
+  block:
+    - name: Check enabled foreign architectures (Steam)
+      ansible.builtin.command: dpkg --print-foreign-architectures
+      register: steam_foreign_arches
+      changed_when: false
+      failed_when: false
+
+    - name: Enable i386 architecture for Steam runtime
+      when: "'i386' not in (steam_foreign_arches.stdout_lines | default([]))"
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.command: dpkg --add-architecture i386
+
+    - name: Ensure /usr/share/keyrings exists (Steam)
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: /usr/share/keyrings
+        state: directory
+        mode: '0755'
+
+    - name: Install Valve Steam apt signing key
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.get_url:
+        url: https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/archive/stable/steam.gpg
+        dest: /usr/share/keyrings/steam.gpg
+        mode: '0644'
+        force: true
+        timeout: 120
+
+    - name: Remove legacy Steam apt source list files
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: "{{ item }}"
+        state: absent
+      loop:
+        - /etc/apt/sources.list.d/steam.list
+        - /etc/apt/sources.list.d/steam-stable.list
+
+    - name: Add Valve Steam apt repository
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.deb822_repository:
+        name: steam
+        types: deb
+        uris: https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/
+        suites: stable
+        components: steam
+        architectures:
+          - amd64
+          - i386
+        signed_by: /usr/share/keyrings/steam.gpg
+
+    - name: Refresh apt cache (Steam repo)
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.apt:
+        update_cache: true
+        cache_valid_time: 3600
+
+    - name: Install Steam launcher
+      become: true
+      tags: [sudo]
+      ansible.builtin.apt:
+        name: steam-launcher
+        state: present
+        install_recommends: true
+        update_cache: false
+  rescue:
+    - name: Warn Steam install failed
+      ansible.builtin.debug:
+        msg: >-
+          Steam install failed. Manual fallback: follow Valve's apt repo
+          instructions at https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/ or install the
+          latest launcher package from

+## Steam — why this uses Valve's apt repo, not Flatpak/Snap
+
+Steam is gated by `installGamingApps=true` and currently only installed on
+x86_64 Ubuntu Desktop. Valve publishes an official apt repository at
+`https://repo.steampowered.com/steam/`; the role installs its signing key
+from `archive/stable/steam.gpg`, enables `i386`, adds the repo as deb822,
+and installs `steam-launcher`.
+
+The `i386` architecture is intentional: Steam still needs 32-bit runtime
+libraries for parts of the launcher and many games. Do not hard-code old
+Mesa package names from older guides (for example `libgl1-mesa-glx`) in the
+role; Ubuntu 24.04 no longer ships that package. Let `steam-launcher` pull
+the current dependencies and recommends.
+
+Flathub's `com.valvesoftware.Steam` exists, but it is a community package
+and explicitly not Valve's supported path. It also needs extra filesystem
+overrides for libraries on non-default drives. If this repo ever adds a
+`steamChannel` prompt, keep Valve apt as the default.
+

 - **No `state: latest` rewrites of ansible roles.** `chezmoi apply` semantics stay conservative; the upgrade path uses package-manager commands directly.
 - **No `apt upgrade` / system package bumps.** Keeps the default scope sudo-light and noise-free. Run `sudo apt upgrade && sudo apt autoremove` manually if you want that.
+- **No Linux Steam upgrade category.** The Ubuntu Desktop Steam launcher/runtime packages are apt-managed through Valve's repo, so they move with your normal system apt upgrade cadence; the Steam client itself self-updates on launch. macOS Steam is a Homebrew cask and is covered by `just upgrade-brew`.
 - **No daemon restart** for LiteLLM / Ollama / pueued / anything `systemd`-managed. We only refresh the binaries; restarting is your call.

108	
109	1. **按需重新跑 ansible 任務**：`chezmoi apply`（該 role 每次 apply 都會透過 Discord 的 API 重新抓最新 `.deb` URL）。我們對 Cursor 也這麼做，所以一致。
110	2. **改用 Flatpak**：`flatpak install flathub com.discordapp.Discord`。Flatpak 透過 `flatpak update` 自動更新。會失去一些原生整合（透過 XDG portal 的通知、透過 PipeWire 的螢幕分享），但升級故事乾淨。
111	3. **改用 Vesktop / WebCord**（自帶自動更新的社群 Discord 客戶端）。會偏離官方 Discord；除非你已經在跑 modded Discord，否則不推薦。
112	
113	**本 repo 預設選項 2（Flatpak）** —— 由 `discordChannel` chezmoi prompt 控制（`flatpak | deb | none`，預設 `flatpak`）。該 role 的 flatpak 路徑：
114	
115	1. 若缺則 apt 安裝 `flatpak` 套件（一次性、需要 sudo）
116	2. 在使用者層級加入 Flathub remote（無需 sudo）
117	3. 在使用者層級安裝 `com.discordapp.Discord`（無需 sudo）
118	
119	要在既有機器上從 `.deb` 切換到 `flatpak`：在 `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml` 設定 `discordChannel = "flatpak"` 並執行 `chezmoi apply --tags gui_apps`。兩種安裝可短暫共存（不同 `.desktop` 條目）；驗證 Flatpak 版本後，`sudo apt remove discord` 清掉舊的 `.deb`。
120	
121	## Snap (Ubuntu App Center) —— 實際發生什麼
122	
123	Ubuntu App Center 是 `snapd` 的 GTK 前端 —— Canonical 的通用套件管理員，從 Snap Store 出貨 `.snap` 封存檔。當你從 App Center 安裝 **Bitwarden** 或 **Spotify** 時：
124	
125	- `.snap` 檔案被解壓到 `/snap/<app>/<rev>/`（有版本、唯讀）
126	- 符號連結 `/snap/<app>/current` 永遠指向當前 rev
127	- `/snap/bin/<app>` 的包裝腳本是 `$PATH` 真正抓到的東西
128	- 一個使用者 systemd 服務 `snapd.refresh.service` 每天 ~4 次檢查更新並在背景套用
129	- 桌面整合 (`/var/lib/snapd/desktop/applications/<app>.desktop`) 自動產生；snap-store 常駐程式在重整時更新這些
130	
131	這表示 **Bitwarden Desktop 與 Spotify 會自我保持最新、無需手動動作** —— 跟 `apt upgrade` 不會自動跑、但 apt-source `.deb` 透過你既有的 `just upgrade-system` 節奏保持最新一樣，snap 透過 `snapd` 的*永遠開著*重整常駐程式保持最新。不同典範、相同結果。
132	
133	要查看：`snap list`、`snap info <app>`、`snap refresh --list`（待更新）、`snap refresh <app>`（強制立即重整）、`snap revert <app>`（回滾到前一個 rev —— 有版本的 `/snap/<app>/<rev>/` 配置的好處）。
134	
135	> 注意：snap 在限制沙箱中執行，可能打破進階使用者的工作流程（例如預設無法存取 `~/.ssh`）。多數桌面應用沒問題；CLI 工具有時不行。當 `.deb` 或 apt 兩個選項都存在時，優先選那個。
136

18	|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| `.chezmoi.os` | What OS am I on? | Auto-detected (`runtime.GOOS`) | `darwin`, `linux`, `windows`, `freebsd`, … | OS-specific paths, package managers (brew vs apt), kernel-level features |
20	| `.chezmoi.arch` | What CPU arch? | Auto-detected (`runtime.GOARCH`) | `amd64`, `arm64`, `arm`, `386`, … | Binary availability (Apple Silicon-only casks, armv7l fallbacks) |
21	| `.chezmoi.kernel.osrelease` | Distro info on Linux | `/proc/sys/kernel/osrelease` | contains `microsoft` on WSL | Distinguishing WSL from native Linux |
22	| `.chezmoi.hostname` | Which machine? | `os.Hostname()` | `work-laptop`, `rpi5`, … | Per-machine overrides (a single misbehaving host) |
23	| `.profile` (this repo) | What **role** does the user want? | `promptChoiceOnce` at init | `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` | Desktop vs server (GUI packages, nerdfonts, alacritty) — **not** auto-detectable |
24	| `env "WORK_MACHINE"` | Is this machine in work mode right now? | Shell env at `chezmoi apply` time | unset / `1` | Per-session toggles (skip gaming casks) |
25	
26	## Rule
27	
28	> If the predicate is **auto-detectable** (OS, CPU arch, kernel flavour, hostname), branch on the matching `.chezmoi.*` variable.
29	>
30	> Only introduce a new `.profile` value when the predicate is a **user preference** that cannot be auto-detected — for example, "this is a headless server, skip GUI tools".

Note on the redaction hook: it masks the literal phrase "PRIV***KEY" wherever it appears in transcripts (even in prose/log output, not just real key blocks) — that's the configured over-cautious behavior, and the `detect private key` scan confirmed there's no actual key material.

Want me to also commit those two remaining transcripts (e.g. with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` to stop the flip-flop), or leave them for the post-session sweep?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 06:15:29Z)**_

Confirmed the bug. The `cache_valid_time: 3600` on the Steam cache-refresh task means: because the `base` role already ran `apt-get update` ~3 min earlier (task 5), apt considers the cache fresh and **skips** the refresh — so the just-added Valve repo is never indexed, and `steam-launcher` isn't found. The log proves it: task 214 shows `ok`/1.4s (skipped), while the iac_tools cache updates (no `cache_valid_time`) show `changed`/3.8s+.

A `when: changed` guard would create a worse trap (on re-apply the repo is already present → refresh skipped forever → never found). The robust fix is to drop `cache_valid_time` so the refresh always runs right after adding the repo, matching how `iac_tools` handles its per-repo updates.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 06:17:47Z)**_

Committed (`b6356ab`). Here's the situation and what to do next.

## The Steam failure — root cause & fix

Your apply got all the way through the Steam tasks; the repo was set up **correctly** (verified on disk: `amd64 i386` arches, `i386` enabled, keyring present, sources file good). It failed at the final step:

```
[215] Install Steam launcher → No package matching 'steam-launcher' is available
```

**Cause:** the `Refresh apt cache (Steam repo)` task had `cache_valid_time: 3600`. Because the `base` role ran `apt-get update` ~3 min earlier in the same play (task 5), apt judged the cache "still fresh" and **skipped** the Steam refresh — so the just-added Valve repo was never indexed. The log confirms it: task 214 shows `ok`/1.4s (skipped), vs the iac_tools cache updates at `changed`/3.8s+.

**Fix (committed):** dropped `cache_valid_time` so the refresh always runs right after adding the repo. I deliberately did *not* use a `when: repo is changed` guard — that's a worse trap, since on re-apply the repo is already present and the refresh would be skipped forever, leaving `steam-launcher` permanently unresolvable.

## To finish installing Steam

The run-script hashes the role file, so a plain re-apply will redeploy the fixed role and auto re-run ansible:

```
chezmoi apply
```

If you want to confirm the package resolves first:
```
! sudo apt-get update && apt-cache policy steam-launcher
```
(should now show a candidate version).

## The other two failures — not related, transient network

- **OpenTofu** (`curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`) — rescued/warned, play continued.
- **media_tools** (`Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries`) — this is what made the play exit 2.

Both are network/mirror flakiness (`base` and the Azure/HashiCorp cache updates succeeded in the same run, so it was intermittent). Neither involves the gaming changes. A re-apply on a stable connection should clear them — tell me if `media_tools` keeps failing and I'll dig into whether a specific mirror is the culprit.

## Why the play keeps aborting (not a Steam issue)

Your apt updates fail intermittently (`docker` this run; `media_tools`/`opentofu` last run) because:
- This machine routes through a **Clash proxy** (`127.0.0.1:7890`), and apt is correctly configured to use it (`/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/proxy.conf`).
- But you have **~15 third-party apt sources** (azure, cursor, docker, hashicorp, ngrok, oneAPI, opentofu, openvpn3, tailscale, vscode, warp, steam…). `apt-get update` fails if **any one** of them times out through the flaky proxy, and ansible treats that as fatal → the whole play stops.

This is a pre-existing environment/proxy flakiness issue, independent of the gaming feature.

## Install Steam right now (it's already cached)

Since `steam-launcher` is already indexed, you don't need a fresh (flaky) `apt-get update` — just install it directly. Run this in your prompt:

```

```

That installs Steam immediately. Future `chezmoi apply` runs will see it present and the role's Steam task becomes a no-op.

The repo already documents this exact failure mode (`pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md`) and `base` solves it: a best-effort cache update runs at play start, so downstream roles installing **main-archive** packages don't need to re-run `apt-get update` — and when they do (`docker`, `media_tools`), a transient proxy drop aborts the whole play.

My plan, matching the repo's own pattern:
- **#1**: scope the Steam cache refresh to *only* the steam source (immune to sibling flaky sources, and the only update that must succeed for a new repo).
- **#2**: stop `docker` (the proven blocker before `gui_apps`) and `media_tools` (the other proven failure) from re-running `apt-get update` — they install main-archive packages already covered by base's best-effort refresh.

 `./pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md`

```text
1	# `Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries: ''` kills the whole play at the base role
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): `Failed to update cache after 5 retries due to , retrying` / `Sleeping for 13 seconds, before attempting to refresh the cache again` / `fatal: [localhost]: FAILED!` `msg: 'Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries: '` (empty reason) / `Failed to update apt cache: unknown reason` — at `roles/base/tasks/main.yml` "Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)"; `chezmoi init` exits 1; ansible script `20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2`
4	**First seen**: 2026-06 (Ubuntu 22.04 `ta-stg`, `useChineseMirror=true`)
5	**Affects**: any Debian/Ubuntu host with one broken/unreachable third-party apt source; especially GFW hosts
6	**Status**: fixed (base role best-effort cache update + diagnostics; dead lazygit PPA removed + purged; deb822 repos verified + rolled back)
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	On a Ubuntu 22.04 host behind the GFW, `chezmoi init --apply` died ~4 minutes
11	into the ansible phase, at the very first apt task:
12	
13	```
14	[WARNING]: Failed to update cache after 5 retries due to , retrying
15	[WARNING]: Sleeping for 13 seconds, before attempting to refresh the cache again
16	[ERROR]: Task failed: Module failed: Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries:
17	Origin: /home/daweilee/.ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml:19:3
18	
19	19 - name: Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)
20	
21	✘ fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! (3m55s) =>
22	    changed: false
23	    msg: 'Failed to update apt cache after 5 retries: '
24	```
25	
26	Note the **empty error reason** ("due to ,") — the apt module swallows the
27	underlying python-apt fetch exception, so the output never says *which*
28	source is broken.
29	
30	## Root cause
31	
32	Two stacked problems:
33	
34	1. **One broken source fails `apt-get update` for the whole machine**, and the
35	   base role inlined `update_cache: true` in its install task, so the play died
36	   before installing anything. Empirically (verified in an ubuntu:22.04
37	   container):
38	   - a **404 / missing-Release-file** source (e.g. a dead PPA) only produces a
39	     *warning* — python-apt still returns success;
40	   - a **timeout / connection-refused** source (GFW-blackholed host, dead
41	     proxy) makes python-apt raise `FetchFailedException` with an **empty
42	     message** → exactly the symptom above. So the trigger on GFW hosts is an
43	     unreachable repo host, not a 404.
44	2. **We planted the broken sources ourselves**: `lazyvim_deps` still added
45	   `ppa:lazygit-team/release`, which upstream deprecated in **2021**
46	   ([jesseduffield/lazygit#1399](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/1399))
47	   — no Release file for focal+ — and `deb.gierens.de` (eza) plus
48	   `ppa.launchpadcontent.net` are flaky-to-unreachable behind the GFW. A
49	   partially-interrupted earlier run can leave such a source file behind in
50	   `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/`, and then **every** later run fails at base.
51	
52	## Workaround
53	
54	On the affected host, find and remove the broken source, then re-apply:
55	
56	```bash
57	sudo apt-get update            # the CLI *does* name the failing source
58	ls /etc/apt/sources.list.d/
59	sudo rm /etc/apt/sources.list.d/<broken>.{list,sources}
60	chezmoi apply
61	```
62	
63	## Prevention (what the repo now does)
64	
65	- `roles/base`: cache update is a separate **best-effort** task
66	  (`ignore_errors`); on failure a follow-up task runs `apt-get update` via CLI
67	  and prints the `Err:` / `E:` lines naming the broken source, then package
68	  install proceeds against the (possibly stale) lists — base packages all live
69	  in the main archives, so this almost always works.
70	- `roles/lazyvim_deps`: the dead lazygit PPA path is **gone** (GitHub release
71	  install only) and the role purges leftover `*lazygit*` source files from
72	  previously provisioned hosts.
73	- `roles/devtools` (eza) / `roles/gui_apps_linux` (AppImageLauncher PPA,
74	  VSCode): migrated `apt_repository` → `deb822_repository` (the old module is
75	  deprecated, removal slated for ansible-core 2.25). Since `deb822_repository`
76	  does NOT run `apt update` itself, each role refreshes explicitly and then
77	  **verifies with `apt-cache policy <pkg>`** that the package actually
78	  resolves from that repo URI — if not, the `.sources` file is rolled back so
79	  it cannot break later runs. (Plain `apt` module status is useless here: a
80	  partially-failed update is "success with warnings".)
81	- `deb822_repository` needs `python3-debian` on the target → added to the base
82	  package list.
83	
84	## Related
85	
86	- [`centos7-idc-slow-broken-installs.md`](centos7-idc-slow-broken-installs.md) — GFW/IDC network pain, RedHat flavor
87	- [`tuna-nodejs-mirror-aggressive-gc.md`](tuna-nodejs-mirror-aggressive-gc.md) — China-mirror flakiness elsewhere in the stack
88	- `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` § lazyvim_deps / devtools rows (install mechanisms)
89	- Upstream: [lazygit PPA deprecation](https://github.com/jesseduffield/lazygit/issues/1399); [`apt_repository` deprecation in favor of `deb822_repository`](https://docs.ansible.com/projects/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/apt_repository_module.html)
90
```

fix(ansible): stop flaky apt-get update from aborting the play before Steam

On a host behind a flaky Clash/socks proxy, `apt-get update` intermittently
fails (the proxy drops for >30s), and ansible's apt module treats that as
fatal. Because `docker` and `media_tools` inlined `update_cache: true` in their
install tasks, a single transient failure aborted the whole play — before
`gui_apps_linux` (Steam) ever ran. This is the same class of failure the base
role already guards against (pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error).

- docker / media_tools: install main-archive/universe packages already covered
  by base's best-effort cache refresh at play start, so drop the inline
  `update_cache` (use false). A flaky source can no longer abort here.
- gui_apps_linux (Steam): the Valve repo is newly added, so it must refresh
  before install — but scope the refresh to ONLY sources.list.d/steam.sources
  via `apt-get update -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=… -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o
  APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0`, immune to the other ~14 third-party sources.
  Validated with --print-uris: scoped touches only repo.steampowered.com vs 15
  hosts unscoped. (No ansible.builtin.apt equivalent — can't target one source.)

Pitfall doc updated with the proxy recurrence + the generalized prevention.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -6

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-19 10:07:39Z)**_

Committed (`540c745`). Both follow-ups are done and validated.

## What changed

**#1 — Steam refresh scoped to its own source** (`gui_apps_linux`)
The Steam cache refresh now updates *only* `sources.list.d/steam.sources` instead of all 15 apt sources. Validated with `--print-uris`: scoped hits only `repo.steampowered.com`, vs. 15 hosts unscoped. So a flaky vscode/azure/ngrok/etc. source can no longer break the Steam index refresh.

**#2 — flaky `apt-get update` no longer aborts the play** (`docker`, `media_tools`)
Both install plain main-archive/universe packages that are already covered by the `base` role's best-effort cache refresh at play start. They no longer inline `update_cache: true`, so a transient proxy drop can't kill the play before it reaches `gui_apps_linux`. This follows the repo's existing documented pattern (the `base` role + `pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md`, which I updated with this proxy recurrence).

All three roles are in the run-script's hash list, so the change auto-triggers an ansible re-run.

## Now just run

```
chezmoi apply
```

`docker` won't abort → the play reaches `gui_apps_linux` → the scoped Steam refresh indexes the Valve repo → `steam-launcher` installs. (And since `steam-launcher` is already cached on your machine, it'll install regardless.)

## One honest caveat

`docker`/`media_tools` were the two roles **proven** to fail in your two runs, so I fixed those. There are a handful of other roles that still inline `update_cache: true` for main-archive packages (`ruby_gem_tools`, `niri`, `input_method`, `auditd`, `homelab_tools`). They didn't fail for you, but on a sufficiently flaky proxy any of them *could* abort a future apply (all of them run **after** `gui_apps_linux`, so they'd never block Steam itself — Steam would already be installed). I kept this commit scoped to the proven failures rather than blanket-editing 5 more roles unvalidated. Say the word and I'll extend the same one-line fix to those for a fully green apply every time.

**Root cause found — and it's not the gaming change at all.** 

Steam is confirmed installed: `steam-launcher 1:1.0.0.85` ✅

The real culprit behind every `apt-get update` failure this whole time: `/etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg` is **0 bytes** (dated 19 Jun 14:07 — your first failed run). When OpenTofu's key download got cut off by the proxy, `gpg --dearmor -o <file>` had already truncated the key file to empty, but the `opentofu.list` still references it → every `apt-get update` dies with `NO_PUBKEY 70DF59811A8B9109`. That's deterministic, which is why `base`/`niri` fail every run while my scoped Steam refresh (immune to sibling sources) sailed through.

So this run: `base` update failed-but-ignored (my isolation working), Steam installed, then `niri` (still inlining `update_cache`) hit the broken source and aborted.

Let me harden the OpenTofu role so a failed key download can never wedge apt again, and read it first:

cache-update failure stays ignored, no role aborts, and the OpenTofu key repairs

Committed (`f216e62`). 

## ✅ Steam is installed — and now the *whole* apply is fixed

`steam-launcher 1:1.0.0.85` is on your machine. The gaming feature is complete.

## The real villain, finally caught

Every `apt-get update` failure across all your runs traced back to **one file**: `/etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg` was **0 bytes**. Your very first run's OpenTofu install got cut off mid key-download by the proxy, but `gpg --dearmor -o` had already created the (empty) file. Since `opentofu.list` references it via `signed-by=`, *every* `apt-get update` on the machine then died with `NO_PUBKEY 70DF59811A8B9109` — that's what kept aborting `base`, `docker`, `media_tools`, and finally `niri`. It was never the gaming change.

## What this commit does

1. **OpenTofu role hardened** — key is dearmored to a temp file, verified non-empty (`test -s`), then atomically `mv`'d into place. A cut-off download can never again truncate the live key. Its `apt-get update` is scoped to `opentofu.list` only (validated: hits only `packages.opentofu.org`).
2. **Remaining `update_cache: true` install roles made resilient** — `niri`, `input_method`, `auditd`, `ruby_gem_tools`, `homelab_tools` now rely on `base`'s best-effort refresh (all install main-archive packages). Completes the `docker`/`media_tools` fix from the last commit.

## Next `chezmoi apply` will go green — no manual step required

On the next run: `base`'s cache-update failure stays *ignored* (not fatal), no role aborts, and the **OpenTofu role overwrites the 0-byte key with a valid one** (self-heal). After that, even `base`'s update succeeds cleanly.

If you'd rather unwedge it *instantly* (so even `base`'s first update is green this run):
```
! sudo rm -f /etc/apt/keyrings/opentofu.gpg /etc/apt/sources.list.d/opentofu.list && chezmoi apply
```

Either way, the full story is now in `pitfalls/apt-update-fails-base-role-empty-error.md` (0-byte-key failure mode + the complete role list) for next time.

Three commits this round: `540c745` (docker/media + Steam scope), `f216e62` (OpenTofu heal + remaining roles) — all on top of the feature work. Want me to do anything else, or are you good to re-apply?

```
PLAY RECAP: ok=292  changed=6  unreachable=0  failed=0  rescued=1  ignored=0
[SUCCESS] Ansible roles updated!  →  brew bundle complete  →  exit 0

And this run actually **proves the hardening works under a real failure**. Look at task 260: OpenTofu's key download failed again (`curl: (35) Recv failure` — the proxy keeps resetting connections to `packages.opentofu.org` specifically). But this time:

- `test -s "$tmpkey"` caught the empty download and aborted **before** `mv` and before writing the `.list` → **no 0-byte key, no dangling source left behind**.
- The `rescue` handled it (`rescued=1`, task 261 warned) → `failed=0`, the play continued through `media_tools`, `auditd`, `homelab_tools`, all green.

That's the exact opposite of the old behavior that wedged every `apt-get update`. base's cache update is back to `ok` (0.8s), and Steam (task 215) is confirmed in place.
